title: Building Your Launch Playbook
description: Master the core frameworks for planning, timing, and measuring successful product launches.

interactions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a launch playbook?

options.text: Replace the product roadmap with marketing milestones
Coordinate cross-functional teams around shared timelines and deliverables
Document every feature for the engineering team
Provide investors with a financial forecast

interactions.teachingPreamble: A launch playbook is a single source of truth that aligns marketing, sales, product, and support around who does what and by when. When Slack launched its enterprise product, it used a detailed playbook coordinating 12 teams across a 90-day window to ensure messaging, enablement, and infrastructure were all ready simultaneously.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company's beta program shows: 200 sign-ups, 45% activation rate, 12% weekly retention at week 4, and NPS of 62. Which metric is the biggest concern before a full launch?

options.text: Sign-ups are too low to draw conclusions
Activation rate below 50% signals onboarding friction
12% weekly retention suggests users aren't finding lasting value
NPS of 62 is below the SaaS benchmark

chartData.title: SaaS Beta Program Metrics vs. Industry Benchmarks

interactions.prompt: When should a company typically begin its beta program relative to the planned general availability date?

options.text: 1 - 2 weeks before GA to build last-minute buzz
6 - 12 weeks before GA to iterate on feedback
Only after GA if initial metrics disappoint
12 - 18 months before GA to lock in pricing

interactions.teachingPreamble: Beta programs serve as a controlled stress test with real users before you commit to a public launch. Figma ran a 10-week private beta for its Dev Mode feature, gathering feedback from 500 design teams, which led to three major UX changes before general availability  -  changes that would have been far costlier post-launch.

interactions.prompt: The three standard launch tiers used in most GTM playbooks are soft launch, ____, and hard launch.

options.text: Limited release
Beta release
Stealth launch
Pre-launch

interactions.prompt: Your fintech product is ready for launch, but a major competitor just announced a similar feature releasing in 3 weeks. You can launch now with minimal PR support, or wait 4 weeks for a full campaign. What do you do?

options.text: Launch now to establish first-mover positioning in the market
Wait 4 weeks for the full campaign and stronger differentiation
Do a soft launch now, then a hard launch in 4 weeks
Delay 8 weeks to add more features and outperform the competitor

interactions.prompt: Which launch metric best indicates whether your go-to-market messaging is resonating with your target audience?

options.text: Total website traffic on launch day
Landing page visitor-to-signup conversion rate
Number of press mentions received
Social media follower count increase

interactions.teachingPreamble: Launch metrics fall into three categories: awareness (reach, impressions), engagement (conversion rates, activation), and retention (DAU/MAU, churn). Dropbox famously tracked its landing page conversion rate during its MVP launch  -  a 35% visitor-to-waitlist rate validated that the value proposition resonated, even before the product was fully built.

interactions.prompt: You're building a launch playbook for a B2B analytics tool. Rank these workstreams from earliest to latest in your timeline: (a) Sales enablement training, (b) Beta user recruitment, (c) Press embargo and PR outreach, (d) Launch day war room and monitoring.

options.text: Sales enablement training
Beta user recruitment
Press embargo and PR outreach
Launch day war room and monitoring

interactions.prompt: Your beta just surfaced that enterprise users love the product but SMBs churn within a week. Your playbook targets both segments with a single launch. What's your best move?

options.text: Launch for enterprise only and delay the SMB go-to-market
Proceed with the unified launch as planned
Cancel the launch entirely until SMB retention improves
Launch for SMBs first since they need more market validation

interactions.priorContext: Your original playbook assumed a single launch targeting both enterprise and SMB segments simultaneously. Beta data now reveals a sharp divergence: enterprise users show 80% retention while SMB users drop to 15% by week two.
